components.name: Risk chip
components.description: Amber appears only for at-risk or attention; on paper it carries dark text.

narrative.overview: The public homepage is a document being made under a lamp. A near-black forest-green field holds one pool of warm light. On it sit aged cream sheets: a run sheet that fills itself, a pair report, a folder of four documents, a sign-off slip. Oxblood wax is the mark layer; amber is not a brand accent, it is an alarm. The audience is the office that runs hostel allocation, so the page behaves like the paperwork they already trust: ruled registers, numbered room cells, a signature line, a floor that is reported rather than averaged. Motion is physical and one-directional; the same page rests in a complete state when motion is unavailable.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black green field with one warm light pool and fine engraved horizontal texture.
Aged cream paper as the object layer; oxblood wax as the mark layer; amber only for risk.
Besley variable serif for display, Public Sans for body, IBM Plex Mono for data.
Pill controls and small-radius paper with offset, soft-blur shadows.
One deterministic sample run drives every figure on the page.

rules.name: The Amber Rarity Rule
rules.body: Amber is reserved for at-risk or attention. If it appears on a healthy room, a decorative glow or a generic CTA, the page has misused it.

rules.name: The Two Pennies Rule
rules.body: Paper is an object, not a card grid. A paper surface must contain information a warden could act on or file; four identical empty cards are not paper.

rules.name: The Data Gets Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is for measurements, identifiers, table values and document labels. It is never the body voice or a decorative 'technical' texture.

rules.name: The Heading Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: No kicker, eyebrow or micro-label sits above an h1 or h2. The heading carries its own weight.

dos: Do keep the field palette scoped to .mm-home; the signed-in admin app keeps its own tokens.
Do put every displayed figure through simulate.ts so pair count, rooms, labels, floor and weakest rooms agree.
Do label every sample figure as illustrative and keep the seeded fixture deterministic.
Do use the margin rail and header progress rule as the persistent thread.
Do give controls 999px radii, visible focus and at least 44px touch height.
Do let paper carry real content: a table, a reason, a floor, an audit row.
Do keep amber for at-risk only.
donts: Don't invent an institute, hall, term, date or academic calendar.
Don't put amber text directly on cream paper; use wax or a dark/amber backing.
Don't add an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't number sections or use a repeated icon + heading + text card as the page structure.
Don't use a repeating grid as texture.
Don't use blur, glass or a zero-offset coloured halo as decoration.
Don't make the homepage depend on auth, the API, a CDN, Google Fonts or any network request.
